utterances.text: All right. Take a look at his photograph and you can tell me perhaps. But may I have the list returned to me because I have some more things on that same page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. May have this piece of paper returned to me, please? And what about this: Do you know that all the persons killed in the centre of town were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I said I didn't know who the persons killed were or the ethnicity of them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I don't suppose you know that they were shot from the sniper nest on the water tower and the roof of the department store where the machine-gun nest was positioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He doesn't know who they were. He doesn't know how they were killed. Now, move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you know -- do you know, for example, that Risto Stevanovic was killed from the Party of Democratic Action premises which are located in Njegoseva number 7, Njegoseva Street number 7 in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I've already said I don't know the names of the persons killed and where they came from or how they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know do you know in the mosque in the centre of town there was also a sniper nest positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, according to Serbian sources, at every ten metres there were sniper nests but that's what the Serb authorities claimed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you say that you don't know how these people were killed or how they lost their lives and you don't know a single Serb who was killed on that occasion, how come you can claim then that the persons who were killed did not take part in any fighting as we're speaking about -- when talking about the Muslims who were killed, for example? How can you say they were civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the people that I mentioned, I said that they were civilians and that they were not armed and that they were not wearing military uniforms but were wearing ordinary civilian clothing. Now, what ethnicity they were, I said I couldn't say either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, Ibrahim Belkic. Do you know that he was killed in battle at the town stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't. I said I don't know the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that Asim Fidahic was also killed at the town park also in battle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. No point reading your list out. He doesn't know the names. He can't help us, so let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But mention is made here of Redzep's house, and we had the opportunity of seeing it on the diagram with the nest and the barricade and that it is in its vicinity that most of the bodies were found; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know that Coso Nargalic was in command of that barricade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know that he was in command, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was at the barricade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know that he was at the barricade either, but he was found in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah, he was found in that location. Now, do you know Amir Besic, nicknamed Begi, the Bay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of a traffic policeman called Beli who from a Muslim village near Ugljevik --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: A traffic policeman you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And his nickname was Beli.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: And you say he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A previous witness, Gusalic, who wasn't a protected witness, claimed that the Muslim forces held control of the area around the hospital for a full three days. Is he not telling the truth? And that that's where most the fighting took place, the barricade around Redzep's house and the whole hospital. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Well, as to the fact that they held it for two or three days, I can't say, I don't know. Now, as to whether there was fighting or not, I don't know that either. All I know is that I was there on the second or third day perhaps after the conflict began.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you can't tell us anything about that. You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that the last question be redacted. It is something that would reveal the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how this can identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to ask any more questions about this? Let's go into private session while the accused asks his questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the operation of the attack against the Serbs was led by Hasan Piric, who was later killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know the man. You hadn't heard that he was in charge of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And had you heard of a unit called Black Swans which was later called after Hasan Piric because he was the founder of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes, I do know of the Black Swans. But who founded them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Well, what do you know about that unit the Black Swans? Was it a unit of paramilitary Muslim extremists or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, that unit belonged to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I think it was stationed somewhere near Sarajevo or in Sarajevo. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that in the settlement Gvozderic, there was a clash among the Muslims themselves and that there were casualties there? Are you aware of that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, conflicts among Muslims themselves in Gvozderic, I'm not aware of that. I know the area well though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's this other one that's been switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that after the situation calmed down in Bijeljina and these 500 long barrels were surrendered that many fled, precisely the organisers of the Hasan Piric operation? And not only did they surrender 500 barrels but they took a lot of weapons with them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of lists of Muslims which had to be arrested, and these lists were in the possession of the police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And are those lists of the people who provoked killings, blockades, killed these persons, and the police drew up a list of names of people that needed to be arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: It wasn't a police list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was the police a multi-ethnic force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: The police was multi-ethnic, but only the Serb policemen had that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Only Serb policemen had the list. How do you know that none of the Muslim policemen had that list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I can only give you an answer in closed session, in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that that last question and answer be redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In one of the questions, we observed that the police in Bijeljina was multi-ethnic; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right then. Now, tell me this -- so we're talking about that area, general area, Bijeljina, Semberija, and the surrounding area. Is it true that the army of Republika Srpska was multi-ethnic too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: At that time, I really can't say. I don't know. I wasn't with the army. But as far as I know, the members of the Muslim -- of Muslim ethnicity in the reserve force of the army refused to mobilise, to go to the mobilisation call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the 3rd Semberija Brigade numbered several thousand fighters and that mostly they were Muslims? Not mostly, but 95 per cent. The 3rd Semberija Brigade of the army of Republika Srpska. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: That might be true, but all I can say about that brigade is that the brigade was composed of people from Bijeljina who were not able or did not succeed in escaping from Bijeljina. So they were mobilised. And while they were on the battlefront, their families were in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say by that that they were in some way forced to join the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. If they could have been -- if they could have been forced to be in the armies could they be forced to be commanders, leaders, directors, managers, functionaries in Bijeljina? Did anybody force them to take up positions of that kind in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know that there were any directors. And if the unit is made up of Muslim forces or predominantly Muslim soldiers, then it is quite normal for the commander to be one of them, one of those member.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you heard about Major Pasaga Halilovic, for example, who was commander of that 3rd Semberija Brigade in question and he was also the director of the Duvan company and is still a director there and is living in Bijeljina? Do you want to say that he and similar people were mobilised by force because their families were in Bijeljina and somebody would have done something to their families had they refused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they had to be commanders forcibly and leaders and directors and all the rest of it, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, if you have been mobilised into the army, the army of the former Yugoslavia, that means you were mobilised for the place you were mobilised for or in. And the same system applied in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that the Chief of Staff of that brigade, for example was Major Sejfudin Buric and he was professor of defence and projection [as interpreted] at the agricultural school as well. Do you know the man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about Captain Sead Tikvesa? Do you know of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know of him either. The only officers that I knew were the former JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, these were as well. They were either active-duty officers or reserve JNA officers depending on their professions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Right. You could know the active ones but you couldn't know the reserve ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How about Jusuf Joltic, have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How will Samir Joltic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Alija Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And Salcin Mehic? What about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No. Those names are not familiar. I can't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm giving you the names of different people who were Muslims from the Muslim community who were in the army of Republika Srpska. What about Alija Durakovic? Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I think that name rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what about Sead Becirevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Salko Dragic, another one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Alija Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Adnan Berberovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: That rings a bell, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ferid Terzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Sejdic, nickname Murge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ferhat Terzic, how about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Tepavcevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Likewise, I don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Muhamed Lipnjicevic, a captain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: It sort of rings a bell but I don't know that he was a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And Smail Candzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I won't read out any more names. You have recognised a few of them. Now, do you think that they were forced, that they were forcibly recruited into the army of Republika Srpska and that they were forced to be its members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, I don't think any of them would have gone voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that Captain Sead, for example, Captain Sead Tikvesa, and a man called Pulja were captured in the battles at Orasje by the other side and slaughtered quite literally? Their throats were cut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As far as I know, one command of the brigade was captured, this Muslim one you mentioned, and that same command was exchanged later on with the authorities of the Republika Srpska. There was an exchange that took place and the people were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The authorities of Republika Srpska exchanged their own soldiers for the soldiers captured from the enemy side, and they exchanged them for the Muslim captives that they had in their ranks. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Orasje, Smail Candzic, and Ramo Durakovic and Jusuf Berisa had all been captured there and Alija Omerovic and Major Sejfudin Buric as well? They were all exchanged in the same way for the members of the enemy side who had been captured. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I said as far as I knew, this same command or however many people there were there asked for an exchange to take place, and they asked to go back to the Serbian side again for the simple reason that their families were there. Their families had stayed behind in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that it was precisely those forces who held the line between Orasje, Loncari, Krepsic, Markovica Polje, Gorica, Vuksic, that general area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that in the units of the army of Republika Srpska, of the guards, the security chief was a Croat, Dusko Tuzlancic, and the head of security in the 2nd Semberija was a Croat as well. Dusko Kondor was his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Who was his wife? Who was he married to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That is what you give as your only explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've got an answer to the witness's question. You have a huge amount of detail. Do you know the wife of Dusko Kondor?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who his wife is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably she's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that or do you just assume it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I assume it. But I think I know so too, although I'm not quite sure. You can check it out yourself, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And I assume that as you are well acquainted with the town of Bijeljina itself, you know that, that's not being challenged, is it? You're well acquainted with Bijeljina. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes, fairly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know the changes in some of the street names in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: At what period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely after the conflicts in Bijeljina. When you say that the Serb authorities and that the Serb authorities were, according to you, nationalists and against the Muslims. Isn't that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: What I know is that some streets changed their names. Which ones exactly, I don't know, but I think that for example, one of the streets which ran -- which stretched towards Amajlije was changed. The name became the JNA street. And there were some other changes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There were changes, but what do you think about the changes that were made, for example, whereby Serb names were replaced with Muslim names? Is that an indicator of any kind of Serb nationalism or does it point to a respect which the two ethnic groups have vis-a-vis each other, especially in Bijeljina? Isn't that an illustration of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Well, all I know is that changes took place. And for example, the JNA Street is no longer called the JNA Street. It is called the Serb Volunteer Forces Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know, for example, that the Braca Jaksic Street, and that is a Serb name, Braca Jaksic, it changed its name to become the street of Second Lieutenant Smajic? That's what it's called.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: What's it called now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I assume it's called the same way now. And do you know that the Patrice Lumumba Street changed its name and became Camil Sijaric Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Well, perhaps at that time its name did change, but what's the situation like now? Is it still named that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, my information is up-to-date. I receive the information now, not then. So I assume they're the same. The Brigade street is now Muslim Brigade Street; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I think that the Muslimanska Brigada or Muslim Brigade Street has another name. Check it out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have the Official Gazette of Bijeljina, the official papers when the Municipal Assembly makes decision of that kind, it decides whether or not to change street names. For example, the Ivan Markovic Street, Irac, Ivana Markovica Ulica changed its name to become Hasan Kikic Street. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: As I say, there were changes. Now, whether those changes have remained to the present day, I'm not quite sure. Because at the end of the conflicts in Bijeljina, there were changes that were made during those two months, as far as I know, but later on I know that they were changed again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've got two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've got quite a lot more questions left, Mr. May. As always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. B-1003, you were told that there was a state of war in Bijeljina. Now, is it true that when you arrived in Bijeljina there was no war there at all at the time any longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Because everything had been completed within the space of two or three days. Everything was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you arrived in Bijeljina on the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you said that when you arrived, there was no war after that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: On the first two days there was some sporadic fire but no serious clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to have to skip some questions which would require private session again. I'm not going to name any names or institutions that you worked in, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I ask that that be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So if it's just one more question that I'm being allowed, then let me ask you this: You were shown a document here which the competent authorities in Bijeljina sent down the vertical line to the authorities of Republika Srpska, and in the document it says as follows, and this was quoted to you, separately quoted. It's not very legible, but in the paragraph that you were quoted, it says that the security situation in Bijeljina was destabilised, had been destabilised in the night between the 31st of March, 1992, when the Muslim extremists set up barricades in the centre of town and that during the night and during the following day, the Territorial Defence and the Serbian National Guard, as well as the Serbian Volunteer Guard, started to dismantle those blockades under the leadership of the Crisis Staff of the Bijeljina municipality. Now, does the fact that the competent authorities are informing their superior organs about the fact that what had happened was that first these blockades had been set up by the Muslim extremists, which the Serb forces then had to dismantle and do away with in order to enable life to return back to normal in Bijeljina, does that testify as to cause and effect, what the cause was and what the effect was? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Just deal with that briefly, if you would.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, from that passage that was read out, there were some barricades. Perhaps that is true, and that the Serb guards or Serb Volunteer Guards intervened. That seems to me to be slightly incorrect, because the interventions undertaken by Arkan's men, it is the Arkan's men who went first. And allegedly those barricades or those points were attacked by them one by one. And as far as I know, that same Serbian guard and the other paramilitary units moved behind Arkan's men and slowly emptied the shops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Tapuskovic, have you any questions for this witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I might need five or six minutes to cover the questions I have in mind which I think would be useful for Your Honours. I'm not quite sure, Your Honours, whether this list of rich, well to do Muslims that existed, according to this witness, were in open session at the time. I think we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said -- we heard what you said during the examination-in-chief, that this was a list of well-off citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina of Muslim ethnicity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in your statement to the investigators, you said that when you returned after the 1st of May to Bijeljina, in the police station you were shown or you heard that there existed an official list of Muslims that were being looked for for certain criminal offences that they had committed. You never mentioned that these were lists of rich Muslims who were suspected of criminal offences. Which is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: The Serb forces had compiled that list of these people, giving the explanation that they had committed crimes, that they were perpetrators of criminal offences. And when you read through that list and review it, you see that these were persons who were rather better off than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I can understand all that, but would you explain to the Court why you didn't say at the time that these were prosperous citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were Muslims? Why didn't you tell them then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And another point. You also said on the 1st of May you had a day off, and then the next day you went to Brcko but you were -- no. You were told by phone to go to Brcko and to stop the looting in the area. First of all, is that the order you received? And who gave you that order to go and prevent such serious criminal offences? Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1003
utterances.text: It came from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the document which you explained to Their Honours today answering questions by the Prosecutor, tab 3, Exhibit 420, it says under point 4 that you explained --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a sealed exhibit, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-1003, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are free to go. I'm going to ask you to remain just for a minute or two while I read something out. It has nothing to do with you at all, but we have to make rearrangements for you to leave, so it's easier if you just remain. I'm going to give an oral ruling in relation to the admission of the evidence of Rule 92 bis witnesses that we discussed last week. It deals with the following witnesses: C-1052, 1063, 1084, 1091, 1140, 1152, 1153. All these statements are admissible under Rule 92 bis. None deal with the acts or conduct of the accused or in any way proximate to him. It is also cumulative in the sense of being evidence of alleged attacks on villages and killings by the JNA and other Serb or Croatian Serb forces. However, the witnesses will be required to attend for cross-examination since their evidence deals with a matter put in issue by the accused, namely the role and the use of the JNA and other Croatian Serb and Serb forces in the attacks on villages and killings. The accused criticised the quality of the statements in his submissions, saying that he had found 38 instances during the course of the evidence where witnesses had disclaimed parts of their statement. But it should be noted that Rule 92 bis provides a safeguard for this eventuality since the Rule requires witnesses to make a written declaration that the contents are true and correct. This entails the witness in checking the contents and making any alterations necessary. We were unable to conclude the remaining witnesses on the list for last week. We will conclude them as soon as we can this week. Perhaps you would pass that on to Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff is out of the office this week. Mr. McKeon will be handling that matter for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McKeon, we will deal with that as soon as we conveniently can. There are, I think, another six and then we need to do another tranche after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: In addition to the other six that were originally on that list, I think there may be two Dubrovnik witnesses that have perhaps been overlooked. That would be C-1197 and C-1210. And I would ask that they could also be considered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will look at those. Do we have videolink tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There are two witnesses scheduled -- their testimony to be taken by videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do they both have to be dealt with tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They're from the same location. One person lives very close to that location, and it could go on -- I don't know if Your Honour is thinking about Wednesday or a day aside from Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tuesday and Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. That would be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just so we know what the time parameters are. Very well. We will adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
